_disclaimer: Illustrative FIXTURE templates for the ayurveda-oncology-support proposal. None of these are patient-visible until an oncology-dietitian approval (plus the same version's clinician/Ayurveda approvals for any herb note) is recorded. No template includes a calorie/protein calculator, a personalized meal plan, or a supplement dose.
review_expiry: review required within 12 months of approval date; no approval date set yet

templates.goal: Support adequate energy and protein intake despite reduced appetite; slow or stop unintentional weight loss.
may_apply_when: reduced appetite during or after cancer treatment
unintentional weight loss not yet formally assessed
unsuitable_when: dysphagia/aspiration risk (use mucositis/dysphagia template and refer for swallow assessment instead)
rapid unintentional weight loss already under dietitian/medical workup -- defer to that plan
templates.flexible_food_pattern: Small frequent energy- and protein-dense meals/snacks rather than three large meals; fortify usual foods (e.g. added ghee/oil, nut pastes, dairy or dairy-alternative, legumes) rather than restricting food groups; fluids between rather than with meals to avoid early fullness.
indian_food_examples: Khichdi enriched with ghee and paneer or moong dal
Full-fat milk or paneer-based smoothies with banana
Idli/dosa with extra ghee or coconut chutney
Roasted nut and seed powder stirred into porridge or curd
Coconut and jaggery-based small energy balls (laddoo) if tolerated and not contraindicated for glucose control
templates.ayurvedic_tradition_context: Some Ayurvedic sources describe agni (digestive fire) as diminished during illness and favor warm, well-cooked, easily digestible food with ghee to support appetite. This is a traditional framing, presented separately, and is not itself evidence of a biomedical appetite-stimulant effect.
templates.biomedical_rationale: Energy- and protein-dense small meals reduce the volume needed per sitting while meeting intake targets; this is standard oncology-nutrition guidance, not specific to any herb.
templates.herb_supplement_note: No herb or supplement is recommended in this template. If a clinician and Ayurveda-clinician jointly approve a specific supportive herb card in the future for appetite, it will be linked here as a separate, independently reviewed item -- never bundled into the food pattern itself.
red_flags_requiring_escalation: weight loss greater than roughly 5% of body weight in a month
inability to keep food or fluids down

templates.goal: Maintain fluid and food intake while nausea is managed by prescribed antiemetics.
may_apply_when: treatment-related nausea with antiemetics already prescribed or being arranged
unsuitable_when: vomiting preventing any fluid retention (needs urgent clinical contact, not a diet template)
templates.flexible_food_pattern: Bland, room-temperature or cool foods with mild aroma; small sips of fluid throughout the day; avoid very fatty, very sweet, or strongly spiced foods if they worsen symptoms; eat before feeling very hungry to avoid an empty-stomach nausea trigger.
indian_food_examples: Plain khichdi or curd rice
Dry toast or plain poha
Buttermilk (chaas) with a pinch of roasted cumin
Coconut water in small sips
Plain, thin dal without heavy tempering if aroma is a trigger
templates.ayurvedic_tradition_context: Ginger and small amounts of dry-roasted cumin/fennel are traditionally used in Indian households for digestive comfort. This is a culinary/traditional note, not a claim that these foods treat chemotherapy-induced nausea.
templates.biomedical_rationale: Small, frequent, bland intake reduces gastric distension and aroma triggers; consistent with standard oncology supportive-care nutrition advice.
templates.herb_supplement_note: Ginger is addressed separately in knowledge/ayurveda-oncology/example_cards.json (card-ginger-cinv-general and card-ginger-ac-null) as a clinician_discussion_only / insufficient_evidence item, never as a substitute for prescribed antiemetics. This food template does not itself recommend a ginger dose or preparation.

templates.goal: Maintain intake safely when the mouth or throat is sore, dry, or swallowing is painful/effortful.
may_apply_when: mild painful swallowing already assessed as not an aspiration risk
unsuitable_when: any suspected aspiration risk or diagnosed dysphagia requiring a speech-and-swallow therapist's texture plan -- defer entirely to that clinical plan
acute severe mucositis unable to swallow saliva
templates.flexible_food_pattern: Soft, moist, lukewarm-to-cool foods; avoid acidic, very salty, very spicy, coarse, or crusty textures; moisten dry foods with sauces, dals, or yogurt; small bites.
indian_food_examples: Well-cooked, mashed khichdi with extra ghee
Curd (dahi) or lassi if not contraindicated
Mashed banana or ripe papaya
Soft idli soaked slightly in sambar or coconut chutney
Pureed dal soup
templates.ayurvedic_tradition_context: Cooling, moist, ghee-based preparations are traditionally favored for irritated tissue in some Ayurvedic dietary frameworks. Presented as tradition, not as treatment for mucositis.
templates.biomedical_rationale: Soft, moist, non-irritant textures reduce mechanical and chemical irritation of inflamed oral/esophageal mucosa; standard supportive-care nutrition principle.
templates.herb_supplement_note: No herb or supplement is recommended for mucositis in this template.
red_flags_requiring_escalation: coughing or choking with food/fluids (possible aspiration)

templates.goal: Reduce stool frequency/fluidity while maintaining hydration and electrolyte intake.
may_apply_when: treatment-related diarrhea without fever or blood in stool
unsuitable_when: fever, blood in stool, or signs of infection (contact clinical team, do not manage with diet alone)
templates.flexible_food_pattern: Low-insoluble-fiber, low-fat, low-lactose pattern temporarily; frequent small sips of oral-rehydration-appropriate fluids; reintroduce fiber gradually as symptoms settle.
indian_food_examples: Plain rice or rice-based khichdi without heavy legumes
Curd (dahi) if lactose is tolerated -- omit if not
Ripe banana
Buttermilk with a pinch of salt and roasted cumin as a fluid/electrolyte source
Boiled and mashed potato
templates.ayurvedic_tradition_context: Buttermilk with roasted cumin is a traditional household remedy for loose motions in many Indian communities. Traditional use noted separately; not presented as a validated antidiarrheal treatment.
templates.biomedical_rationale: Temporary reduction of insoluble fiber and fat, plus oral fluid/electrolyte replacement, is standard supportive management for treatment-related diarrhea pending medical review if it persists.
templates.herb_supplement_note: No herb or supplement is recommended in this template.
red_flags_requiring_escalation: known or suspected neutropenia with fever (medical emergency)

templates.goal: Support comfortable, regular bowel movements while explicitly screening out obstruction before any fiber/fluid advice is applied.
may_apply_when: mild treatment- or opioid-related constipation with no obstruction red flags present
unsuitable_when: any obstruction red flag below is present -- this template must not be shown or followed if so
known bowel surgery/stoma without surgical team clearance for dietary fiber changes
obstruction_red_flags_screen_first: no bowel movement or gas passage for several days with worsening pain
templates.flexible_food_pattern: Gradual increase in fluids and soluble fiber if no red flags are present; regular meal timing; light activity as tolerated.
indian_food_examples: Well-hydrated whole fruits such as papaya or pear
Soaked and cooked whole moong or chana in moderation
Warm water first thing in the morning
Vegetable-forward dal with skins retained where tolerated
templates.ayurvedic_tradition_context: Warm water and well-cooked legumes are traditionally favored for regularity in some frameworks. This is a general, non-forced dietary note -- it explicitly excludes any laxative-herb, purgative (virechana-style), or cleansing regimen, which are out of scope for this module.
templates.biomedical_rationale: Gradual fiber and fluid increase is standard first-line dietary management for uncomplicated constipation once obstruction has been excluded.
templates.herb_supplement_note: No herbal laxative, purgative formulation, or supplement is included or implied. This module explicitly excludes virechana, forced-purgation, and similar self-directed cleansing practices for people with cancer.
red_flags_requiring_escalation: any obstruction red flag listed above
no improvement after a few days of the flexible pattern

templates.goal: Reduce foodborne-illness risk during neutropenia or substantial immunosuppression.
unsuitable_when: not currently neutropenic/immunosuppressed -- do not apply unnecessarily restrictive food-safety rules outside this window
templates.flexible_food_pattern: Well-cooked foods only; avoid unpasteurized dairy and juice, raw or undercooked meat/egg/fish, raw sprouts, unwashed raw produce, and buffet/leftover food held at room temperature; wash hands and produce thoroughly; use safe water.
indian_food_examples: Well-cooked dal and vegetables instead of raw salads
Pasteurized milk/curd instead of unpasteurized
Freshly boiled and cooled water or well-boiled soups instead of raw fruit/vegetable juices
Fully cooked khichdi instead of raw sprouted-lentil (moong/chana) salads
templates.ayurvedic_tradition_context: Not applicable as a distinct tradition item here -- this template is safety-driven; any traditional raw-food, raw-sprout, or raw-juice practice is explicitly set aside during neutropenia regardless of tradition.
templates.biomedical_rationale: Neutropenic patients have materially higher risk of severe infection from foodborne pathogens; raw sprouts, unpasteurized juices/dairy, and undercooked animal products are established higher-risk items in oncology food-safety guidance.
templates.herb_supplement_note: No herb, supplement, or raw herbal juice/concoction is recommended during neutropenia in this template.
red_flags_requiring_escalation: fever during known or suspected neutropenia (treat as a medical emergency, not a diet question)
any GI illness symptom during neutropenia
templates.audit_note_from_local_diet_chart: The local 'LIFE SUPPORT DIET' handout recommends raw soaked nuts, raw sprouted legumes, and multiple raw vegetable/fruit juices multiple times daily with no neutropenia screening. That pattern is flagged as unsafe during neutropenia and is NOT reproduced here; see source-assessment.md.
